title.narrative: Provide increased access to Education and Protection Mainstreaming in Rural Damascus and Aleppo

description.narrative:
ltpgtltspangtHNlt/spangtltspangtO 2023 estimates that 15.3 million people need help (47% of them children), with the highest proportion in Aleppo at 2.8 million and in rural Damascus at 2.6 million. Human and economic indicators continue to deteriorate, and basic services are collapsing. The deteriorating situation is exacerbated by the ongoing outbreak of cholera and other epidemics and basic services such as electricity, combustion, fuel and other infrastructure are near collapse, including schools, which have suffered destruction and lack of basic equipment, such as electricity, mattresses, and educational means, this affected negatively the educational process and increased children's dropout rate. The HNO 2023 report indicates that more than 2 million children in Syria are out of school during 2023.lt/spangtltbrgtlt/pgt
ltpgtIn this project, which will be implemented within a full year, it will contribute to the humanitarian response plan within the education sector. SSSD will target the most dangerous areas on the scale of the 4-severity scale. As the education and protection sector reports indicate, 8 selected schools will be rehabilitated in coordination with the MoE and planning directorates in the governorates of Aleppo and Rural Damascus. (2 schools in Meskanah, 6 schools in Mleiha) Schools will be lightly rehabilitated, water and sewage systems will be maintained, schools' classes will be provided with tables, seats, as well as boards, and teachers' supplies and 4 schools (2 schools in Meskanah, 2 schools in Mleiha) will be provided with a solar power system, where more than 5,000 students will benefit.lt/pgt
